objective: Test and replace the unjustified single-center matroid exchange premise by exact multi-center localization, with explicit positive root-domain control graphs.

atomic_claims.text: For every m>=2 the displayed order-6m simple 3-connected cubic graph has a feasible center set isolated under all single exchanges, another at distance two, and at least 3^m feasible center sets.
The actual feasible P3-center sets need not satisfy the matroid basis-exchange axiom, as witnessed by the two displayed factors.
For a private-endpoint center set, changing r centers localizes every factor change inside at most 6r vertices, comprising the touched center-matching pairs and their endpoints.
A forest has at most one P3-factor; hence the private-endpoint setting requires girth(G)<=6r for every different feasible center set at distance r.
Local tests of G_2,...,G_10 and exhaustive center-subset comparisons for G_2,G_3 agree with the stated constructions and obstructions; this is not a graph-order census.

assumptions: Finite simple cubic graphs; 3-connected means vertex connectivity at least three.
P3 components are selected two-edge paths, not necessarily induced.
Private-endpoint localization assumes that every vertex has exactly one neighbor in the initial center set; this is not assumed for all root graphs.
risks: The family consists of positive root instances; the obstruction is only to the specified center-exchange premise.
No arbitrary-high-girth family with this partition is asserted; the girth bound is conditional.
Local code is not committed; the full recurrence is given in the proof and code/output hashes are retained.
No canonical ledger, legacy DAG dependency or Result is edited; transport is not mathematical Evidence.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: The explicit G_2 has feasible C={8,9,10,11} and C*={0,5,10,11}, but every one-center exchange from C fails domination. Thus feasible center sets are not universally matroid bases on V(G). This does not negate root.
